description: Documented flood-affected locations in Bengaluru during the October 2024 rain events that fall within the five UrbanFLOW Bengaluru model catchments (HSR, Koramangala, Bellandur, Whitefield, Electronic City). Every incident corresponds to a location named in a verifiable news report; each entry carries its source URL, publication date, and the event it belongs to. Coordinates were geocoded from OpenStreetMap (Nominatim). No flood depths, incident counts, or control-room records are asserted that are not present in the cited sources.

events.name: October 14-15, 2024 heavy-rain flooding

observed_rainfall.note: 65 mm city-wide between 8 am and 8 pm on Oct 15 (BBMP / New Indian Express); 228% above seasonal average. Waterlogging reported at 142 places; 52 areas and 142 houses flooded; 34 places declared flood-prone by BBMP.

events.summary: Citywide waterlogging and IT-corridor disruption after a 65 mm day: Silk Board, Madiwala, Sarjapur Road, HSR Layout flyover, Electronic City, and Whitefield all reported in traffic-police advisories.

events.name: October 19-20, 2024 overnight flooding (south and west corridors)

observed_rainfall.note: Kengeri 141 mm (BBMP sources quoted by TOI); Jnana Bharathi, RR Nagar, Nayandahalli 106 mm; IMD Bengaluru city station 19.7 mm. Hosur Road at Roopena Agrahara and Silk Board Junction were reported flooded.

events.summary: Overnight rain left Hosur Road (Roopena Agrahara), Silk Board Junction, Varthur-Gunjur Road, ITPL Road and the Mysuru Road corridor waterlogged until mid-morning.

events.name: October 21-22, 2024 record cloudburst (India Meteorological Department GKVK 186.2 mm)

observed_rainfall.note: IMD GKVK station recorded 186.2 mm, the highest single-day October rainfall for Bengaluru in 27 years (previous record 178.9 mm on Oct 1, 1997). BBMP reported 157 mm over six hours in the Yelahanka zone; the city received 264.5 mm up to 8:30 am on Oct 22. Revenue Minister Krishna Byre Gowda described a 'cloud-burst-like' situation. Two lakes (Kogilu, Doddabommasandra) breached; NDRF/SDRF boats were deployed at Kendriya Vihar; ~100 lakes were reported overflowing.

events.summary: The record October cloudburst flooded the southeastern IT corridor: ORR service roads between Iblur and Marathahalli (with slow traffic near Ecospace junction), Bellandur Lake overflow onto ORR service roads, and 'roads turned into rivers' in Sarjapur, Bellandur, Devarabeesanahalli, HSR Layout and Karthik Nagar near Marathahalli.
